items.title: Outstatic: Authenticated GitHub REST proxy can send OAuth token to non-GitHub origins
items.description:
Impact
Outstatic’s authenticated GitHub REST proxy accepted an unvalidated endpoint parameter and constructed an upstream GitHub API URL by string concatenation while attaching the authenticated user’s GitHub OAuth token.

A user with access to the Outstatic dashboard could craft a request that caused the server to send their own GitHub OAuth token to a non-GitHub host. If that token was captured, it could be used to access GitHub resources available to that same user, including private repositories depending on granted scopes.

This does not allow unauthenticated attackers to access private repository data, and it does not directly expose another user’s GitHub token without an additional same-origin execution or request-forging primitive.

items.title: cassandra-jdbc-wrapper: Authentication Token Exposed in Logs
items.description:
Summary
The fix for AIKIDO-2024-10565 (https://intel.aikido.dev/cve/AIKIDO-2024-10565) (plaintext password logging) introduced two
redaction helpers — DriverUtil.toStringWithoutSensitiveValues() and
DriverUtil.redactSensitiveValuesInJdbcUrl() — but both helpers only redact
the "password" property/parameter (JdbcUrlUtil.TAG_PASSWORD). The equally
sensitive "token" property (JdbcUrlUtil.TAG_TOKEN), used for DataStax
Astra and other token-based Cassandra authentication, is completely unredacted
by both helpers. Applications using token-based authentication with DEBUG
logging enabled will therefore log the live authentication token in plaintext
via SessionHolder's calls to these same two helpers — the exact same
exposure pattern that the original fix was intended to prevent.
